ref: Diagnose possible substance misuse / depression / anxiety / burnout in health worker with occupational stress
text: The four possible-diagnosis rules are byte-identical in their evidence: (and Stress-at-work (or <all 19 screening findings>)). The page's column structure is flattened away, so 'Fatigue' alone yields possible substance misuse, depression, anxiety and burnout at once, and the column heading 'Possible alcohol or drug problem' (which is itself a 'possible X' conclusion attached to only its own four findings) is not preserved. The footer's 'any of the above may have ...' justifies a broad reading, but a closer encoding would evidence substance misuse from the alcohol/drug column (with the others as broad fallbacks) so the specific conclusion the page draws is kept.

ref: Check for urgent features and signs of occupational stress in the health worker (check_for)
text: Two screening items are absent from the check_for and therefore from every rule: 'Diagnosis of long-term condition' (representable, e.g. Chronic disease + New qualifier) and 'Frequent lateness' (no SNOMED concept found; a not_representable note is the appropriate handling).
The footer names five conclusions (substance misuse, stress, depression, anxiety, burnout); 'stress' has no possible-diagnosis rule. Low because the trigger is already 'Stress at work'.

Every rule is anchored on (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Stress at work" "finding")), which is not a recorded common symptom or warning sign, and nothing else on the page records it. The page is also about the health worker, not the patient, so whether these rules can ever fire in a patient encounter is a question for the clinician/remaining-questions file. Not a wrong encoding, but the house standard asks for this to be flagged.

ref: Urgent: health worker with occupational stress ... (red box)
text: All four red-box criteria are qualified 'at work' on the page; no item carries that context. The language has no clean way to express it (an 'Occupational' qualifier value exists but is not an established pattern), so this is a limitation to record rather than an error.
An 'event'-category concept inside clinical_finding. The grammar's category validator accepts it, but no gold-standard rule does this; confirm the runtime records and matches it.

Each requires 'Stress at work' AND any one of the identify-stress indicators, but the page uses those indicators to identify occupational stress itself; a worker with mood change but no prior stress finding gets no diagnosis. Circular trigger.

ref: possible substance misuse / depression / anxiety / burnout
text: Identical 19-item OR lists on all four; no differentiation by symptom group (alcohol items for substance misuse, mood for depression/anxiety, performance for burnout). Over-triggering.
Missing 'Diagnosis of long-term condition' and 'Frequent lateness' items; the urgent items are included in check_for as intended.
No diagnosis for 'stress' though the page lists it among likely conditions.

Each rule requires 'Stress at work' AND one of the signs. On the page, these signs are how occupational stress is identified ('Identify occupational stress in yourself and your colleagues'), and the conclusion applies to 'the health worker with any of the above'. Requiring a prior 'Stress at work' finding is circular: a colleague showing these signs without a recorded 'Stress at work' finding never triggers the rules.
